findings.problem: The question says Jesus stayed in "that tomb", pointing back to the tomb on story card 12, which is no longer on screen. The question should say which tomb, for example the tomb where they laid Jesus after taking Him down from the tree.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The question asks how the Gentiles react when they hear Paul and Barnabas "say this". "This" points back to the Scripture quote on story card 9, which is no longer on screen. The question should say what they heard: that Paul and Barnabas are turning to the Gentiles, and the line about a light for the Gentiles (Acts 13:46-47).

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: No story card sets up the prophets' warning in Acts 13:40-41. Card 18 is a choice card, and the setup only appears inside the question on card 19. A story card should tell the warning first. The rest of the warning in 13:41 (wonder and perish, a work they would never believe) is never told anywhere either.

rule.text: The setup for a choice is always on a story card.

findings.problem: Acts 13:50 says "They stirred up persecution", but it leaves open who "they" are: the Jews, or the women and leading men they incited. The question settles it as "The leading men and prominent women of the city stir up persecution." The question should keep it open, for example "Persecution is stirred up against Paul and Barnabas."

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The right answer "The One God raised from the dead" is a description that echoes the setup and the quote on card 15. Both wrong answers are named people ("Samuel the prophet of Israel", "Saul son of Kish from Benjamin"). So the right answer is a different kind of thing and stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The right answer "They rejoice and glorify the word of the Lord" uses the Bible's wording. The wrong answers are plain modern phrasing ("ask for a sign before they will listen", "stay quiet and wait for the leaders"). That makes the right answer sound more like the Bible than the others.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The joke calls John Mark "the John who went home". Acts 13:13 says only that John left them "to return to Jerusalem". It never calls Jerusalem his home.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: "I've been forgiven for a lot of crooked stamps" adds something new to Papa Dorin's backstory. In the backstory his stamps came out crooked and the family switched to a new stamper. Nobody forgives him in it.

rule.text: He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: God's testimony about David in Acts 13:22 is never told: 'I have found David son of Jesse a man after My own heart; he will carry out My will in its entirety.' It is a key detail of the sermon, and it leads into Jesus coming from David's descendants in 13:23. Card 7 asks only who God raised up, and card 8 moves on.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
